T15: holding the liquid ETF plus the BUY indices in the OUT-SELL regime (the three-index switch OUT and MAUc1 SELL)

Test T15, run headline; descriptive, no null, no chance claim (waiver); findings PROVISIONAL at most; pre-registration sha256 343566ddab004aa6; windows W1 and W2 with their own dates throughout. Contents: answer, data, one backtest, D-table and ledger, curves, robustness, definitions.

1. The answer

Question. In the weeks when the three-index switch is OUT and the MAUc1 gold signal is SELL (the OUT-SELL regime), does holding the liquid ETF plus each index whose own SIGN is still BUY, in equal parts (-idx), change what the switch earns, on both base sleeves (50/50 and 80/20), on W1 and W2? The comparisons are descriptive: -idx against the original rule (C1 CAGR, C2 worst fall), against holding only the liquid ETF in the regime (C3) and against half parent + half GOLDBEES (C4), 16 comparisons in all (T15.md 2.3).

What this page can and cannot say. There is no null, no random draw, no percentile and no p-value in T15 (Manu's waiver, 2026-11-25), so no claim about chance or skill is made. A PASS means only that the stated difference had the stated sign in at least 3 of the 4 books over the seen weeks. The four books are one market seen four times: in OUT-SELL weeks -idx holds the same indices and cash in every book, so their agreement is close to automatic. Both windows were seen before the variant was proposed (post-hoc), there is no hold-out, and choosing the best of the eight rules from these tables is a selection on seen data. Findings are PROVISIONAL at most (T15.md 2.2); the verdict wording below is the pre-registered outcome map (T15.md 2.5) applied mechanically.

4 of 16 comparisons pass (a pass = the stated sign in at least 3 of the books), after 20.8 bps, whole window.

The largest caveats (T15.md 3, known contaminants):

  • The index leg is a price index with no dividends and no fund cost, not a tradable instrument: a real index fund or ETF would differ by roughly the dividend yield minus its costs, and Smallcap 100 / Midcap 100 funds were thin or absent in 2014-2019. R5 tests the cost side only (0.5 pp a year); the dividend side is not run (no approved dividend series).
  • The effective sample is the index-holding spells (the independent unit for the change): W1 (T11's / T14's inputs): 6 index-holding spells in 33 index weeks; the largest single spell holds an index in 9 of them; W2 (T08's / T14's inputs): 6 index-holding spells in 22 index weeks; the largest single spell holds an index in 10 of them.
  • The four books are one market seen four times, with one in-or-out series and one gold series; in OUT-SELL weeks -idx holds identical indices and cash in all four, so "3 of 4" is a consistency check, not four tests.
  • W1's parent is rebuilt from the parent's baskets and Eikon prices, not validated against a published NAV before 2019-01-02 (no published series exists before 2019-01-02); nine manual Eikon exports for delisted stocks (provenance unrecorded) supply bars in W1; both windows are seen; the variant, the rule's weights and the MAUc1 signal were chosen after seeing 2014-2026 results; cash is 1/3 to all of the regime holding, and the cash file's source before 2026-08-10 is unrecorded (F-AA-D09).

3. One backtest, end to end

One book (the first), one window at a time, rule 50-idx at 20.8 bps, from the signals to the statistics, with the formulas and the real numbers from trades.csv. A reader with a calculator can redo every step. The trade rows are read from the evidence by a fixed rule (the first such trade of the book), and the page says which.

7. Definitions, formulas and how to reproduce

nav

NAV_t = cash_t + Σ_i units_i × close_i,t over the parent's stocks, GOLDBEES and each of the three indices (Nifty 100, Midcap 100, Smallcap 100: units × the index close; on a calendar session with no index bar the last close is carried); cash = LBES units × LBES level; base 1.0 at the close of the first session; daily marks on the book's sessions; units are constant between trades

cost

at a trade session (the session after the decision), at its fill prices (stocks OHLC4, GOLDBEES de-spiked OHLC4, cash at its level, each index at its own OHLC4): V = value of every line; target value of line i = target share_i × V; traded = Σ over every line (stocks, GOLDBEES, cash, each index) |target value_i − held value_i|; cost = traded × cost_bps ÷ 2 ÷ 10,000 (10.4 bps a side at 20.8 bps; 0 and 50 bps as robustness); every target is then scaled by (V − cost) ÷ V, so line i after the trade = target share_i × (V − cost) units_i = value after ÷ fill price_i; shares after cost = value after ÷ (V − cost)

regime

at a weekly decision (the last session of each ISO week, and T0): the latest Master row of each index and of MAUc1 dated on or before the decision date; IN = all three index SIGNs BUY; OUT-BUY = not IN and MAUc1 SIGN BUY; OUT-SELL = not IN and MAUc1 SIGN SELL. B = the indices (Nifty 100, Midcap 100, Smallcap 100) whose own SIGN is BUY at the decision; k = |B| (only B read in OUT-SELL; at most 2 there, since 3 BUY is IN)

targets

target shares of the book at a decision (parent / GOLDBEES / cash / each index): all rules, IN: parent 1. -orig, -liq, -half OUT: T14's (e, gw): parent e, GOLDBEES (1 − e) × gw, cash (1 − e) × (1 − gw); 50-orig OUT-BUY and OUT-SELL: GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5; 80-orig: OUT-BUY GOLDBEES 0.8, cash 0.2, OUT-SELL GOLDBEES 0.2, cash 0.8; -liq OUT-SELL: cash 1; -half OUT-SELL: parent 0.5, GOLDBEES 0.5; -liq and -half OUT-BUY as the base sleeve. 50-idx, 80-idx: IN parent 1; OUT-BUY the base sleeve (50/50: GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5; 80/20: GOLDBEES 0.8, cash 0.2); OUT-SELL: cash 1 ÷ (k + 1) and each index in B 1 ÷ (k + 1), no parent, no GOLDBEES. A trade is due on the session after decision j iff the target differs from decision j − 1's; for -idx the target includes B, so a change of B inside OUT-SELL is a trade

cagr

CAGR = NAV_end ^ (252 ÷ (sessions − 1)) − 1 (sessions = the book's trading sessions in the window; years = (sessions − 1) ÷ 252; arithmetic, price return, after the stated cost)

maxdd

max drawdown = min over t of ( NAV_t ÷ max(NAV_s, s ≤ t) − 1 ) (negative; 'shallower or equal' = closer to 0 or equal, by the unrounded value)

calmar

Calmar = CAGR ÷ |max drawdown|

vol

volatility = standard deviation (n − 1) of the daily NAV returns × √252

diff

difference = statistic(A) − statistic(B) on the same book, window, cost and cash leg; CAGR, max drawdown, volatility and cost paid in pp (a positive max-drawdown difference = shallower); Calmar as a number; trades as a count; cost paid = Σ of the costs of the run's trades as a share of the starting NAV 1.0, shown in pp

cmp

C1: CAGR(b-idx) > CAGR(b-orig); C2: max drawdown(b-idx) ≥ max drawdown(b-orig); C3: CAGR(b-idx) > CAGR(b-liq); C4: CAGR(b-idx) > CAGR(b-half); by the unrounded statistics, per book, after 20.8 bps over the whole window. n = the number of books in which the condition holds; the comparison PASSES iff n ≥ 3 of the books. No null, no draws, no percentile, no p-value: a pass describes seen weeks and is not a claim about chance.

ledger

ledger return of an instrument or rule over a span = value_end ÷ value_start − 1, from the close of the session on which the span's first decision is traded (T0 for decision 0) to the close of the session on which the decision that ends it is traded (or the last session); an OUT-SELL spell = a run of consecutive OUT-SELL decisions; a stretch = a run inside it with the same B; parent = hold the parent (0 bps); Nifty 100, Midcap 100, Smallcap 100 = the hold-the-index NAV (index close ÷ index close); each rule = its own NAV at 20.8 bps; GOLDBEES and cash = close ÷ close from the evidence's ledger

cmix

constant mix at a rule's own averages: each line's share = the mean over the weekly decisions of the rule's target share (f_parent, f_goldbees, f_cash, f_index), rebalanced at every decision and every basket change; shows how much of a difference is only a different average exposure

state

sessions held in a state = the sessions of the book's calendar whose held target is that regime (and, in OUT-SELL, that k): a decision's target is held from the close of its trade session (the next session after the decision), T0's target from the first session

r4

R4, leave one spell out: for OUT-SELL spell s, a run in which -idx holds B = the empty set (cash only, as -liq) on spell s's decisions; C1-C4 recomputed with the run's -idx against the headline's comparators; 'flips' = the comparisons whose PASS / FAIL differs from the headline's

r5

R5: every index OHLC4 and close of session i is multiplied by (1 − 0.005 ÷ 252)^i (i counted in sessions of the window's calendar from T0), a fund-cost drag of 0.5 pp a year on the index leg; dividends (the opposite side) are not run; R2: LIQUIDCASE as the cash leg (W1 whole window; W2 from 2024-01-24); R3: W1 from 2015-01-02, W2 live decisions from 2021-11-01, each starting in its own first state

Reproduce

From AA/: bash tests/T15/run.sh regenerates the evidence, the gates, analysis.log, this page and its check (python tests/T15/report.py --run headline, then python tests/T15/check_page.py --run headline, which re-derives every number and every date on this page from the raw evidence files and exits 1 on any failure). No draws are made and no seed is used.

Pre-registration: sha256 of T15.md §1-§3 343566ddab004aa6 (recomputed from T15.md; match with the header: True); the audit.json of each window carries the same hash. METHODS.md beside this page.
